info.album: My Boy Lollipop: The Best Of Millie Small

podcast.body: Released in early 1964, this song became a massive international hit, reaching number two on the charts in both the UK and the US, launching Millie into stardom. Chris Blackwell chose this song, remembering it as a sound system favorite, and commissioned Ernest Ranglin to arrange it. The backing was performed by Jimmy Powell and the Five Dimensions, with a harmonica solo replacing the original saxophone solo to align with British chart trends; Millie consistently claimed Rod Stewart played this harmonica part. "My Boy Lollipop came out in early 1964 and became a massive hit, reaching number two on the chart both in the UK and the US, and Millie was now a star."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: This song became a worldwide hit, serving as the "big breakthrough" for Ska (SCOP/Blue Beat) music in Britain. Produced by Chris Blackwell and distributed through his new Island Records label, its success helped spread Jamaican music further into the mainstream and among white British youth, particularly mods. "The big breakthrough was a worldwide hit by Millie Small, called My Boy Lollipop, produced by Englishman Chris Blackwell, and distributed through his brand new Idle and Records label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
